EICMA 2026 • Triumph TF-E Bikes Get Even More Enduro With Updates for the 2027 Model Year
Hyundai Shelves the N Vision 74 Indefinitely
12 photos
Photo: Hyundai
The Hyundai N Vision 74 was confirmed for production in August 2024, and we were all waiting to see the firm’s first real supercar. However, it turns out that we have been waiting in vain, because Hyundai shelved the radical project indefinitely.
Hyundai has officially shelved production plans for the N Vision 74 , confirming that the retro-futuristic hydrogen coupe will not be built for the foreseeable future. Hyundai Design Center chief Simon Loasby revealed that the automaker simply could not make the financial math work.
Loasby explained that evaluating the car solely on its expected sales volume and direct impact left it with "no chance" whatsoever of turning a profit. Even when factoring in its potential as a halo car, the financial case still fell short.
The decision comes after Hyundai invested serious effort and money into the project following its debut back in July 2022 as a high-performance "rolling lab" concept and its confirmation for production in August 2024. Hyundai filed trademarks for the model in August 2026. The automaker has reportedly built several prototypes and completed a full-production-ready clay model of both the exterior and interior.
Photo: Hyundai However, something happened along the way, and the executives decided to pull the plug on what might have been Hyundai’s first production supercar. Speaking to The Drive at a media preview for the launch of the 2027 Hyundai Elantra , Simon Loasby revealed that the model slated for production before the end of the decade is no longer coming.
The N Vision 74 was supposed to hit the market powered by two electric motors, mounted out back, and featuring a hydrogen fuel cell and a battery with a capacity of 62.4 kWh. Hyundai claimed the car could drive as far as 373 miles (600 kilometers)l.
Sitting on an 800-volt architecture, the dual-motor powertrain produced 671 horsepower (680 metric horsepower) and 664 pound-feet (900 Newton meters) of torque, which would have pushed it from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in under 4.0 seconds and on to a top speed of 155 mph (250 kph).
The N Vision 74 may be shelved, but Hyundai has big plans for the near future. The first step was the official unveiling of the new-generation Elantra both as a pure ICE with the 2.0-liter inline-four, coming next year, and as a hybrid with the 1.6-liter four-cylinder engine working alongside an electric motor, ready to hit the market in 2028. An N variant is expected to drop in the lineup at a later date.
Photo: Hyundai As for the N Vision 74 supercar, Loasby left the door cracked, saying, " At the moment, no ," in a conversaton with The Drive. That sounds like the model might go into production when the market conditions are kinder to hydrogen-powered cars.

EICMA 2026 • Benelli Showed the World Its New Tornado Naked Tre 903 Concept at EICMA 2026 and It's a Triple!
Black Friday for Riders: Take a Look at a Few Brands With Massive Sales on Their Phone Mounts
20 photos
Photo: Quad Lock
Imagine riding down the highway on a motorcycle, suddenly receiving a phone call, and having to dig it out of your pocket in order to answer. Not only is this a difficult endeavor if you’re wearing jeans, or any pants, for that matter, but it’s downright dangerous, forcing us to take our eyes off the road, even for a split second; it’s all it takes to be the victim of an accident.
So, over the years, there have been countless brands that sought to solve this very issue, among others, developing countless mounting systems to secure your phone within sight and granting us the ability to keep an eye on our calls, messages, Google Maps, Waze, and countless other uses we have for our modern pocket-sized computers.
Well, with Black Friday underway for countless brands all over the world, I’ve decided to bring to light a few brands that build some of the world’s most trusted motorcycle phone mounts and have ongoing Black Friday sales on their goodies.
Quad Lock Quad Lock is one of those teams that really needs no introduction, having been around since 2011 and climbing to international recognition across a wide range of disciplines, be it motorcycles, dirt bikes, or even just good old cycling.
Photo: Quad Lock I decided to place them in the spotlight first as I recently had an encounter with the brand at EICMA where we also took an interview with brand ambassador Charley Boorman, the one and the same that stars in the Long Way Round series with Ewan McGregor.
It was at EICMA that Quad Lock also launched their all-new Pro Adjustable mount, a piece of gear which I personally saw in action and which allows riders to place their phone in whatever position they like, and it stays that way. All you need is a hex key to make the adjustments and lock the whole thing in place.
This brand currently offers 30% of their entire lineup of gear, including chargers, dampers, and even the anti theft screw kit; ALL OF IT! The new Adjustable mount is priced differently all over the world, but in the US, it’s $63 and fits with the existing phones cases in the Quad Lock lineup.
This brand has been and is responsible for some of the most dependable handlebar mounts around, one that have resisted accident after accident and spill. Riders, Boorman included, proclaim that after an accident, the mounts and their phone were fine, even though they weren’t.
Ram Mounts Up next on our list of brands with hot prices on their gear is none other than Ram Mounts, the one and the same that is often spotted battling it out with Quad Lock as the best around. The thing is that, for Black Friday, this brand doesn’t appear to be tampering with prices all over the world, only in some regions. You’ll need to check with local distributors to unlocks prices of up to 20% on their gear.
Photo: Ram Mounts Their X-Grip Universal phone holder is a product that can be acquired for around $40 and since you’ll also need an actual mount, the Tough Ball, Claw (depending on mounting system chosen), and/or others, be sure to weigh your options and look for the best deal around at this time.
Peak Design Another team that people have talked about, including out very own Mircea Mazuru , is Peak Design, a brand that offers a wide range of mounts and cases for countless applications, and ones that work with magnets and a click-in system, depending on the mount, of course.
Photo: Peak Design Here too, the amount of cash you’ll be saving on the Black Friday deals will matter on where you are in the world, but as an idea of what to expect, we can see reductions on items of as much as 35%, sometimes more, depending on what product you’re interested in.
I’m currently stationed over in Europe, and out here, the SlimLink Motorcycle Mirror Mount is going for just €114, down from €190, and including a built-in charging option for your phone.
Rokform Rokform is a team that, according to their Facebook page, has over 198K followers, so clearly, we can’t leave this brand out of the mix here. They offer a similar mounting system to Quad Lock with a four-point, rotate and lock action that does require a special phone case to work, just like most brands out there.
For Black Friday, this team is offering price reductions that may not be as large as those we see for Quad Lock and Peak Design, but they are still there and Rokform is considered a brand with dependable products.
Photo: Rockform As an idea of what we can save with Rokform, their handlebar phone mount with vibration dampener kit is going for $130 instead of $150. The ball phone mount is $175 instead of $200. Phone cases, however, don’t appear to be seeing any price reductions, at least, not for use riders.
SP Connect Last on our list but not least is SP Connect, a brand whose gear I’ve tested on a bicycle. However, they also make mounts for motorcycles, and one that riders do enjoy. This brand is currently offering a 30% reduction on all their gear too, so very Quad Lock-like.
Photo: SP Connect This brand’s Moto Mount 3D is currently up for grabs at $90, but with the promo code, comes down to close to $70, and the Stem Mount Pro is set for $75 and down to $50 with the code. Don’t forget about cases too, selling for a pre-code price of as low as $45.
This brand also requires that you buy a special case, so be sure to choose the right setup for you.
All in All While these are clearly not the only mounting brands the motorcycle rider can call upon, they are some of the most appreciated and worthy of being on your radar, especially in this time of price reductions.
If you’ve been looking for new mount to help you keep an eye on your smart device as you’re riding around town, some highway, or in the middle of nowhere, this is the time to explore the market offerings.

EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
Owner Bought This 1957 Chevy Bel Air Nomad in 2023, Drove 200 Miles, Sold It for $66,000
29 photos
Photo: Cars and Bids
Just 200 miles in three years. That’s a "garage queen," no matter how you look at it. In an era when station wagons are an endangered species, the gorgeously styled 1957 Chevrolet Bel Air Nomad shows that wagons were once stylish family haulers.
A station wagon from 1957 just hits different. Sure, we still have the BMW M5 Touring , and we had the Audi RS6 Avant, which brought performance in the form of family cars. While they are fast, safe, comfortable, and innovative in their own time, they don’t have the character of the past. And definitely, they don’t have the fins.
This 1957 Chevrolet Bel Air Nomad screams character, all wrapped up in the vintage design from nearly 70 years ago. Finished in the striking Matador Red, one of the most iconic paint colors of the Tri-Five era, and contrasting India Ivory, it features a color-coordinated interior and rides on 14-inch wheels, coming from an era when big wheels were not even a thing.
The car is powered by a Chevrolet Performance crate 350-cubic-inch V8 engine, featuring FiTech throttle body fuel injection, but the listing doesn’t reveal how much the V8 makes right now. Back in 1957, Chevrolet did not have a 350-cubic-inch engine in the lineup. The largest power plant available for the Bel Air Nomad was the 283-cubic-inch small block.
Photo: Cars and Bids The 350 was not introduced until 1967, with the arrival of the Chevrolet Camaro. Under the hood of the Camaro, the 350 pushed out 295 horsepower (299 metric horsepower) and 380 pound-feet (515 Newton meters) of torque.
The restoration experts left the 1950s vibes unaltered, both inside and out. A factory-style Wonder Bar AM radio with Bluetooth connectivity and Vintage Air AC made their way into the cabin. Power windows, power seats with retrofitted lap belts, and an aftermarket front center armrest with cupholders are also on the menu.
The classic two-spoke, thin-rimmed steering wheel with a full chrome horn ring and a Bel Air center cap/emblem frames the speedometer, which is scaled up to 120 mph, and the five-digit odometer, which reads 12,132 miles (19,525 kilometers). That, however, might actually be 112,132 miles (180,459 kilometers).
The one who just sold the car drove only 200 miles (322 kilometers) over the past three years. That is probably just going up and down the trailer for maintenance trips or car shows. The owner listed it for sale on Cars and Bids and, a week later, he closed the deal at $66,000, which is under what such cars sell for on the collector market.
Photo: Cars and Bids So will the new owner park it and drive 200 miles in the next three years, or will they turn it into a daily driver? We’ll probably find out next time the 1957 Chevy Bel Air Nomad is auctioned off.

EICMA 2026 • Honda Africa Twin Gets Biggest Refresh in a Decade, They Now Call It CRF1150L
New Gran Turismo 7 Weekly Challenges and Time Trial to Keep Us Busy Until Spec IV Part 2 Arrives
24 photos
Photo: autoevolution
I have been bombarded with clips, photos, stories and review of GTA VI over the past 24+ hours. Everyone’s got something to say about it, and it’s not always a positive take. I have no opinion on the topic yet and will refrain from one until I get to play it myself.
Until then I can tell you Assetto Corsa Rally has got a new update with two spectacular cars and one seriously challenging rally stage (Sweden!). It might not sound like much if all you care about is how much content a game gives you access to.
But if you prefer having an ultra immersive and intense experience, I can tell you that AC Rally is a great place to be in. If you’re serious about driving, you’ll love it but there’s a downside as well. It will probably ruin any other racing title for you.
Playing Gran Turismo 7 after Assetto Corsa Rally felt like a walk in the park, and I don’t mean in a positive way. It’s still sort of fun if you just want to unwind, but the stakes are so low that it makes you think if it’s genuinely worth your time.
I’m probably still playing it because of how easy it is for me to just sit back and use my controller, as it will take me a few more months to get a proper sim rig setup for a deep dive into both AC EVO and AC Rally.
Sunday Cup Photo: autoevolution I obviously wasn’t keen on downgrading from a Lancia Delta S4 rally car to some boring 380 PP road going vehicle, especially since Tokyo Expressway – Central Clockwise would take ages in the latter.
I know we’re only looking at two laps here, but my 692 bhp Nissan Skyline GT-R (R33) was beckoning to stretch its legs. My only challenge for this first event was not hitting the slower cars from behind, given that their lines can be a bit strange at times.
It wasn’t a problem after 23 seconds, though, and the whole race only took less than three minutes. Being careful means you get an extra Clean Race Bonus, adding up to a total of 40,500 credits. Then there’s also the 100K bonus you get for podiuming in the first event.
You’ll get another 200K for three events, and a 6 Star Roulette ticket after completing all five of them. That was my main incentive for the Weekly Challenges to begin with.
Historic Sports Car Masters Photo: autoevolution Historic Sports Car Masters consists of five events. You either have to race for one lap at the Nurburgring Nordschleife, three at Spa-Francorchamps, or five at Goodwood, Willow Springs and Grand Valley South.
Typically, winning the latter will add 55,000 credits to your virtual account, but I scored 82,500 thanks to another Clean Race Bonus. Mind you, this is the reverse layout of the track we’re talking about, which doesn’t show up as often as the regular version. Hitting the brakes hard after the tunnel can send you sideways, and it happened to me on every lap in the Porsche 959 .
It was great drifting practice for sure, and it made me think I should spend more time inside this car over the next few weeks. It still has the green look I like so much and that I also used for another car in today’s story. Driving this also reminded me that Christoph Mader is working on another Porsche book after the 964 Carrera RS, and this one will revolved around the 959.
Anyway, I took the lead three laps after the start of the race, with two more to go. I saw a few De Tomaso models along the way, and you can see some photos of the Pantera I recently unboxed for a Hot Wheels focused story. You’ll need about seven minutes or less for the whole event, but at least the next one is quite a bit shorter.
Special Event Photo: autoevolution This week’s Special Event is another Time Trial. Funnily enough, it uses the same car manufacturer has the official, Online Time Trial. I’m talking about the Suzuki Vision Gran Turismo, which only weighs 2,138 lbs (970 kg).
It uses a Suzuki Hayabusa engine and three electric motors to achieve AWD and a maximum output of 426 bhp. I prefer the Group 3 racing version, but we can’t choose the cars we want for these events.
It would be nice if Polyphony introduced the option for people to vote on the next car/track combo though. Anyway, you know the drill for the Weekly Challenges Time Trials: we only get to drive on one sector of the track (Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve on this occasion), which means you could theoretically move on after just 60 seconds.
The fastest lap time when I signed in was 42.667, while the target for Gold sits at 45.400. I barely got it on my second attempt, with 30,000 credits waiting at the other end.
Hypercar Parade Photo: autoevolution Hypercar Parade is a slightly more complex “championship” with nine events in total. Racing at Le Mans will unlock the most credits (115,000) with only three laps to cover, while Monza offers the least impressive payout (85,000 credits) after five laps.
Yas Marina Circuit is obviously the latest addition to the program, as it arrived in Update 1.69, and you can score 90,000 credits in roughly 10 minutes (depending on your car of choice). I’m sure most people would say the Ferrari Enzo is “just” a supercar and not a hypercar, but the one I have is pushed to the limit with all the weight reduction packages available in the game and 958 bhp on tap.
And I still think it looks stunning in green with yellow wheels. It can hit 340 kph down the main straight at Yas Marina, and the Yangwang U9 that was leading the pack quickly became a distant memory.
I’ve overhead some people saying that a faster version of that car will be arriving in GT7 next month. Is anyone genuinely excited to hear that? Anyway, my fastest lap in the Enzo was a 1:51.246, which is roughly four seconds slower than the Renault Espace F1 world record from back in Spec III.
World Touring Car 700 Photo: autoevolution I’m not a huge fan of Yas Marina, so I was happy to advance to Mount Panorama for the last event in the Weekly Challenges “program”. I would have preferred being able to race a GT3 machine instead of a GT4 model, and I figured choosing the Ferrari 458 was the only way to make things a bit spicier.
I could’ve even installed a turbocharger and still not be well within the PP rules, but didn’t do it this time. I was already up in P5 after the first lap, and the “guy” in the lead had the same Suzuki from the new Time Trial.
You can go for a one pit stop strategy in this seven-lap race, and I’m almost certain RS tires could work without giving you a headache. After taking the lead my only objective was to improve my lap time, and I found myself going from a 2:22 to a 2:18 and then a 2:16.724 on the final lap.
Not only did I win 165,000 credits, but I also banked one million more from the 6-Star Roulette ticket. I just need 16 million for my next Legendary vehicle.
New Time Trial Photo: autoevolution I went in for a fast lap here just before the Weekly Challenges, and it went poorly. It wasn’t even enough for the Bronze Record Reward, which sits at just under one minute and 30 seconds per lap.
Meanwhile, the fastest drivers in the world are already at 1:21.xxx, which is slightly mind blowing. I’m not a fan of the Suzuki Swift Sport KATANA Edition Gr.4, especially around a high speed track like Tokyo Expressway.
The BoP rules only make it worse by reducing the horsepower and adding more weight. I’m also not fully familiar with the Central Counterclockwise layout which means I am still just reacting to the corners ahead.
There is absolutely no room for error, as hitting the walls will immediately invalidate your lap. I stopped afer 10 of them, settling for a 1:28.655 that might just be slightly above the average lap time.

EICMA 2026 • Yamaha Births New Adventure Scooter Family, Three RW Models That Look More Like Motorcycles
New VW ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Is All About the Present and Future of the Brand's Supermini Hot Hatch
10 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
There have been several important premieres this week, and while some of them were celebrated at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show , others were simply unveiled over the World Wide Web, as that’s a lot cheaper, not to mention that the reach is pretty much the same.
One of them was the Lamborghini Temerario Spyder, the brand’s first-ever supercar to feature a power-folding hardtop, and to be honest, it did not get much traction in our news feed. Hyundai has a new Elantra in its lineup, Honda presented an updated version of its Civic Type R, alongside the Type R HRC Concept, and there is a new Honda Avancier, too, among a whole bunch of other things.
Mind you, the Temerario Spyder wasn’t the only big premiere of the week that enthusiasts do not seem to care about that much, as the same goes for one particular Volkswagen. It’s none other than the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport, and unlike its non-Clubsport sibling, you cannot buy this one. Well, not yet anyway, because it is nothing more than a mere concept at this point, though it could preview an upcoming Clubsport version of the brand’s supermini electric hot hatch.
That’s what the rumor mill says anyway, and to be honest, we wouldn’t be surprised if Volkswagen decided to keep it as a concept. After all, it wouldn’t be the only GTI study that did not offer a glimpse of something more special. You do remember the W12-650 from almost two decades ago, and the GTI Roadster Vision Gran Turismo from 2014, don’t you? None of them made it to production, by the way.
Photo: Volkswagen This two-door concept looks a lot more aggressive than the regular Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI . The Clubsport has two fewer doors, features a vented hood, a big spoiler at the rear, fat wheel arches, and a few other special changes. The livery is also exclusive to the concept, alongside the retro-inspired alloys, and so on. And for what it’s worth, it kind of looks like something that would feel at home in the WRC world, which is a compliment, by the way.
The changes continue on the inside, where it features Recarco bucket seats and five-pointed harnesses, as well as a real roll cage. There are no back seats anymore, and ArtVelours microfleece fabric can be seen in the cabin. The tablet infotainment screen is still a thing, because apparently VW couldn’t make do without it.
Based on the same MEB+ platform as its production sibling, the VW ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept features an electric motor that drives the front wheels, just like the regular ID. Polo GTI. However, the motor powering the study was sourced from the RWD ID.3 Neo GTI and the ID.7, so it brings a heck of a lot more power. Like 63% more. The output is now rated at 362 hp (270 kW/367 ps) as opposed to 222 hp (166 kW/226 ps) on the production model.
During the short acceleration bursts, the show car is said to unleash 389 hp (290 kW/394 ps), allowing this one-off VW GTI to hit 62 mph (100 kph) in 4.7 seconds, or 2.1 seconds faster than the ID. Polo GTI. The top speed is 155 mph (250 kph). And let’s not forget than no ICE-powered GTI drops below the 5-second zone, as the only one that does is the AWD Golf R, which has 329 hp (245 kW/333 ps) to play with.
Photo: Volkswagen Volkswagen’s new ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is the latest model in a string of cars that is all about the brand’s GTI celebrations, as 2026 marks the 50th anniversary of the original Golf GTI . Between us, it definitely looks like something that the automaker could easily put into production as a more upscale version of the EV-powered supermini hot hatch.
If it does indeed hit the assembly line, then chances are it will have a five-door body, and it likely won’t look as aggressive as the study. The bucket seats, harnesses, and roll cage should also be scrapped, and the back seat reintroduced. On top of these, we wouldn’t be surprised if it did not use the punchier electric motor, though that’s pure assumption at this point.
In conclusion, as we previously mentioned, there is no word on whether Volkswagen indeed plans to launch a Clubsport version of the ID. Polo GTI or not, so we cannot tell you if such a thing will get the green light for production. It would indeed be an interesting addition to the brand’s GTI family, and just like the regular hot hatch, it would be kept away from our shores, so the only way to admire it in America would be from the World Wide Web.
Should VW launch an ID. Polo GTI Clubsport in your opinion? And if so, should they bring it to our market, too? Tell us all about it in the comments area below.

15-YO Pizza Boy Got a '69 Mach 1 in 1983, Made It Into a Wheelie-Popping Racer, Beat His Own Shelby
65 photos
Photo: Facebook/Shelby Thurman
In 1905, Gennaro Lombardi popularized coal-oven pies on Spring Street in Manhattan, establishing Lombardi's as the landmark widely celebrated as America's first pizzeria, selling whole pies for 5 cents. Simultaneously in Detroit, Ford Motor Company was building its 1905 lineup, led by the $2,000 four-cylinder Model B, the $1,000 Model F touring phaeton, and the $950 opposed-twin 10-hp Model C capable of a brisk 30 mph.
Nobody in 1905 expected a Ford to haul mozzarella across town at felony velocities. Dedicated American pizza delivery did not truly arrive until around 1950, pioneered by trailblazers like Casa D'Amore in Los Angeles and Pizza King in Dallas. By the 1960s, suburban sprawl, television dinners, and Domino's Pizza—founded in 1960 with its famous 30-minute delivery guarantee—cemented doorstep pizza delivery as an unmistakable pillar of American popular culture.
Decades later, one Tennessee teenager took that 30-minute promise personally and turned it into the world's fastest pepperoni shuttle. Meet Steve Thurman of Portland, Tennessee, as he tells his story to Erik Larsen on the Heart and Horsepower YouTube channel. Needing extra cash after washing cars at Baker Motor Company, a Buick dealership in Gallatin, Thurman moonlit at Domino's, delivering hot pies in a roaring 1969 Ford Mustang Mach 1 .
Delivering pies in a classic Mustang beat flipping burgers by a mile, especially once Thurman memorized every Friday and Saturday regular. Spotting an order for the Jones family, he blasted straight to their porch in record time, pocketed a generous tip, and promptly hijacked his leftover minutes on the clock to cruise town with his buddies. Rolling back into Domino's, his amazed coworkers heard the same cheeky report: delivered early, paid well, no problem.
Photo: Facebook/Shelby Thurman Today, that former teenage delivery rocket looks less like a salami courier and more like a blacked-out menace itching for a green light. Wearing glossy black paint, “Steve Thurman Performance” door lettering, and a pinned matte-black scoop hood, the 1969 Mach 1 sits on massive Phoenix F/X slicks beneath back-halfed quarters. Behind the firewall, the cabin is completely stripped, outfitted with Lexan windows, gutted doors, a full roll cage, racing gauges, and an electronic delay box.
Even Thurman's pre-run ritual drips with deadpan drag-strip humor. Popping the hood exposes a gleaming mechanical fuel injection hat that racers lovingly call "the toilet," which he dutifully wipes clean with a rag before flipping the fuel switch. Waking the barn in Portland with a violent, ground-shaking lope, the bar-less Mach 1 refuses to even contemplate traction on cold garage concrete, casually blowing its oversized slicks off before it ever sees a starting line.
Remarkably, Thurman has owned this Mustang continuously since 1983, a 43-year saga sparked by a lucky family trade at age 15. Back then, young Steve owned a gutted 1965 Mustang mid-restoration that his father desperately wanted, while his uncle parked this running blue 1969 Mach 1 in his driveway. Jumping at the swap, Steve added wheels, tires, an interior, and a stereo, roaring into high school the instant he turned 16 with a legitimate hot rod.
Photo: YouTube/Heart and Horsepower To appreciate what Thurman carved into a drag warrior, consider the towering heritage behind the galloping pony badge. Debuting in April 1964, the Ford Mustang invented the affordable American pony car and triggered a showroom stampede that has now spanned seven distinct generations. Sales-wise, nothing ever matched the original first generation built from 1964½ through 1973, which moved an astounding 2,981,259 units in the United States—peaking at 607,500 cars in 1966 alone.
By 1969, Ford gave the first-generation Mustang a wider, longer-hooded restyling and cranked out 299,824 units across three core body styles. Hardtop coupes led the charge with 150,640 built, encompassing standard, deluxe, bench-seat, and 22,182 luxury Grandé trims. Open-air convertibles were scarce at just 14,746 units, while the sleek SportsRoof fastback accounted for 134,438 cars—highlighted by 72,458 newly introduced Mach 1 models alongside 1,628 Boss 302 and 857 Boss 429 homologation specials.
Engine choices in 1969 epitomized Detroit excess, spanning ten configurations from 115 hp to 375 hp. Buyers picked 200- or 250-cubic-inch sixes (115 hp and 155 hp), a 302 V8 (220 hp), 351 Windsor V8s (250 hp and 290 hp), a 390 V8 (320 hp, 10,464 built), 428 Cobra Jet V8s (335 hp, 13,261 built), or the homologation Boss 302 (290 hp) and Boss 429 (375 hp).
Photo: YouTube/Heart and Horsepower Three transmissions backed those motors: a standard 3-speed manual, an optional 4-speed manual required on both Boss models, and the 4-speed Select-Shift Cruise-O-Matic automatic—pairing the C4 with smaller engines and the C6 with big-blocks. As a Mach 1, Thurman's car originally packed Ford's standard 351-cubic-inch Windsor V8, factory-rated at 250 hp (in two-barrel form) or 290 hp (with the four-barrel carb).
Following his drag-racing father's footsteps, Thurman began uncapping headers and bolting on slicks, soon winning his very first night after wiring in a delay box. That winter, buddy Rodney McCall back-halfed the chassis and welded the cage—back when nobody panicked about cutting up a 1969 Mustang . Today, that original stock 351 block is stroked to 414 cubic inches with an Eagle crank, Eagle rods, Mahle pistons, Trick Flow heads, and methanol-fed Enderle injection.
Burning methanol keeps the stroker cool and dead consistent through muggy Tennessee summers without even needing a cooling fan. Power flows through a trans-brake BTE Powerglide and BTE converter to a 9-inch Ford rear end packing steep 5.14 gears, controlled by four-corner double-adjustable shocks that Thurman dialed in himself.
Photo: YouTube/Heart and Horsepower Before those adjustable shocks arrived, the fresh 414 staged a terrifyingly funny stunt at Bowling Green. Launching hard, the Mach 1 hiked its nose skyward and stayed airborne even after shifting gears automatically. Peeking sideways at half-track without wheelie bars, a rattled Thurman tapped the brakes, landing in a shower of sparks past his stunned rival.
Today, it carries controlled wheelies past 60 feet—right after Thurman's favorite part, a roaring line-lock burnout. And that’s only because Steve is taking it easy – on the car, on himself, on the sport itself. If he really buried his foot in it, and pulled all the stops on the car, his Mach 1 would do a quarter-mile run perfectly vertical, headlights pointing straight at the sky. No wheelie bars, as we can plainly see in the video.
More than iron and methanol, this Mustang anchors a generational Blue Ova l obsession. Thurman's passion for Ford never stopped at the drag strip, the garage, or even the realm of automobiles—he literally named his daughter Shelby, stamping Mustang royalty straight onto the family tree. During the Heart and Horsepower shoot, Steve uncovered a 20-year-old photograph of baby Shelby beaming inside the Mach 1, and she happily climbed back in to recreate the exact pose.
Photo: YouTube/Heart and Horsepower Their bond shines brightest at the strip, where father and daughter trade friendly smack talk as rivals. Representing Team Music City against Shelby's Team Ethridge, they staggered staging lanes to avoid meeting early, only to clash in the finals—where Steve took bragging rights after an eager Shelby red-lighted. Probably the most bitter-sweet victory of his career.
Ask if he would ever sell the Mach 1, and Steve refuses flatly: Shelby would kill him, because someday, the world's fastest pizza car is hers. After all, she’s known this amazing machine her whole life (she’s 21), and there’s now way in heaven that she’s letting go of it.

Digital Lamborghini Espada Would Make the Grand Touring Coupe Proud of a Virtual Spiritual Successor
8 photos
Photo: uygarspots / Instagram
Lamborghini is telling us to save the date because on November 18, 2026, the Sant’Agata Bolognese-based Italian automaker will probably reveal the open-top Temerario derivative, the Temerario Spyder.
The company still hasn’t named the car , but it’s not going to take long before the mystery is cleared – a blue-tinted teaser shows a bit of the car without openly revealing the model. But the rumor mill firmly believes it’s the roofless supercar, their first open-top with a V8 since the 1988 Lamborghini Jalpa.
So far, the family has included the coupe model featuring the Revuelto’s three electric motors, combined with a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 for a total of 907 horsepower, and they also added just recently the Temerario Tettonero model with five striking dual-tone contrast paint options along with a new Akrapovic exhaust system. All of these could line up for the new Spyder, of course.
But what if people also want Lamborghini to look back to its glorious past a little? Just recently, a small firm called Caven Atelier worked with none other than Fabrizio Giugiaro, the son of the iconic Giorgetto Giugiaro and also the designer behind the original Lamborghini Gallardo for the Italian company while he was working at Italdesign during the late 1990s.
Named Hommage 26, this project that will be made in just 25 examples challenged the storied designer to return to the beloved Lambo Gallardo and make it enticing for the late 2020s. The styling is pretty obviously a refresh, but it does come with cool features like pop-down headlights, active aero flaps at the rear, and loads of personality.
As such, it’s really no wonder that someone has now thought about bringing back to life more iconic Lamborghini models from the past – even though only virtually, since we’re dealing with folks who reside across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI, aka the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators.
More precisely, Uygar, a "professional daydreamer" based in Turkey and known as ' uygarspots ' on social media, has taken note of the all-new direction of Lamborghini and decided to swing them around with a retro-focused unofficial, hypothetical design project – the revival in modern key of the Lamborghini Espada four-seat grand tourer.
The original coupe had a different style from other Lamborghini models of the era, as it was styled by Marcello Gandini at Bertone, drawing inspiration from the styling company’s own show cars, making the Espada quite unique to behold. Now, the pixel master strives to rekindle the original style while also implementing the novelties of the late 2020s.
It’s not an electric model, by the way, as clearly hinted by the quad exhaust outlets, but it does open up new possibilities for the company – even though only digitally. We also like the combination of orange for the exterior and blue velour for the interior. How about you? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Uygar (@uygarspots)

Transformer T2 Camper Is Versatility Manifest – Lives up to Its Name and Serves Almost Any Purpose
14 photos
Photo: RD Trailers
Generally, travel trailers follow established design rules, but every once in a while, we come across a trinket that redefines how we approach glamping, and one RV that does just that is none other than Transformer T2 from RD trailers.
Campers, especially smaller ones, are usually governed by construction rules and when a camper goes against the grain, so to speak, and offers something different, we need to be all eyes and ears. Even more so considering the price of a standard T2.
According to the manufacturer’s website, the camper before us is priced starting at just $16,500 (€15,000), and since RD Trailers is one of those smaller teams, you can actually talk things over directly with them to craft the T2 of your dreams, which will clearly depend on the sort of lifestyle you’d like to live while out and about.
Photo: RD Trailers Now, those rules of construction and design which I mentioned mainly refer to how this thing is built and what tricks it has up its sleeve. At the heart of the T2 sits an aluminum frame with sidewalls that are welded directly to that frame. Sealing the sides in is a one-piece fiberglass floor and roof construction, so don’t worry about the elements seeping in.
Because of all this aluminum, the T2 is also rather light, rolling in with a dry weight of 1,500 lbs (680 kg) and able to handle a whopping 3,500 lbs (1,587 kg), granted by the presence of a torsion axle which can be upgraded.
The resulting abilities of the all-aluminum build, insulated sidewalls, and one-piece roof is that water and dust should have a hard time making their way inside your unit, but it also means one very strong construction, especially for the weight. There aren’t a whole lot of campers out there that can handle more than their own weight in cargo.
Photo: RD Trailers Speaking of cargo, it’s in this department that we also witness one of the tricks up the T2’s sleeve. If you’ve had a chance to peek at the images in the gallery, you’ll have spotted the fact that there’s a rear hatch in the T2’s construction, aside from two side doors.
Usually, these hatches hide kitchens, ones equipped with the necessary tools and systems we need to wash and clean dishes and veggies, toss on a couple of eggs and bacon, and even listen to music or fiddle with systems.
Well, you can forget all about this picturesque kitchen, and instead, be prepared to access the actual interior of this camper, directly from the rear. Just keep in mind that it’s NOT a downward opening gate, but a side-action one, so you won’t actually us it as a ramp to stuff items into your unit.
Photo: RD Trailers Instead, it will make for some of the best views from bed that a camper of this size can offer. Just point the rear toward east or west, depending on if you want to see the sunrise or sunset and just wait for the magic to happen.
Another benefit is that, yes, you can easily cram larger items into your camper including e-bikes, kayaks that’ll fit, and more. In essence, the T2 is a tailer that can be whatever it is you want but does start off without a mattress, so it’s more of a toy hauler, than anything else. Again, only in its more standard layout.
In truth, there isn’t anything in the spec sheet or options list about a bed, but that’s easily resolved with a modular mattress that you can find after your purchase, or tap into the E-tracks that run along the sides to whip up a unique bedding system. You don’t need much and can see the steps necessary here . Look into the skylight option if you do take this route.
Photo: RD Trailers Keep in mind that, due to the amount of cargo the T2 can handle, RD Trailers does invite owners to tap into the roof rack and free up the space inside with a roof-top tent. A great option to ensure you leave the interior untouched, but which does limit the camping seasons in which you’ll feel comfortable. Step-on fenders are in place to access roof-mounted gear and most tents do come with ladders.
While there is no galley in the T2 , all except a dry sink and swing-out system for a Blackstone grill, there is plenty of space for you to craft your own and bring along a fridge, cooktop, spice stash, and more.
Some features that are in place as standard include charge ports, CO2 detector, lights, an AGM battery, and plenty of space for the rest. Shore power is there too, and things like bike mounts can be added, not to mention solar power, annex bathrooms, and batwing awnings to offer shade all around the unit.
While we could talk about the T2 and just how far we can take one for a few hours, it’s best that I leave some details to your discovery and urge you to get in touch with RD Trailers if you’re looking for camper versatility manifest.

EICMA 2026 • Honda Has a Taste of the e-MTB World with the RN0 Motor-Assisted Bicycle
Volkswagen ID. Every1 Virtually Morphs Into the ID. Up! and the GTI Version Also Comes Forward
9 photos
Photo: kdesignag / Instagram
Volkswagen AG launched the ID. series more than half a decade ago as their next-generation family of battery, plug-in hybrid, and extended-range electric cars primarily using the dedicated MEB all-electric platform.
The namesake Volkswagen brand introduced the series as its first purpose-built electric vehicle family with the ID.3 hatchback, and the family has grown to include a multitude of vehicles of all shapes and sizes, both offered into series production and as concept cars. There are even models that have already left their life – like the ID4. and ID.5 crossover SUVs. That’s because Volkswagen is welcoming a new age for the series, where the numbers are replaced with more common denominators – like the ID. Polo and ID. Polo GTI, the newly launched ID. Cross, as well as the larger ID. Tiguan .
The series has grown extremely vast, by the way, as the models that are sold in Europe or North America are also joined by a variety of China-focused nameplates that will probably never reach the Old Continent or American shores. Anyway, with all the commotion going on, it’s no wonder the rumor mill keeps a close eye on them.
According to the latest reports, the next introductions for the ID. series could be the Volkswagen ID. Up! or Lupo, set to become the tiniest member of the family, as well as another China-dedicated model. Now, the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI have also joined the chat, this time around focusing on the potential Volkswagen ID. Up!
More precisely, Kleber Silva, a Brazil-based virtual artist known as " KDesign AG " on social media, has decided to have a CGI go at imagining the return of the small VW passenger car as a direct follow-up to the A-segment Volkswagen ID. Every1 hatchback concept, introduced for the first time during the spring season of 2025 and expected to enter production sometime in 2027.
This could become both the smallest and most affordable Volkswagen in the ID. series, and the company might choose to give it a known name like the Up! or Lupo to keep in line with the new nameplate strategy. The pixel master has gone with the Volkswagen ID. Up! nameplate for this unofficial, hypothetical design project, by the way, and we don’t mind.
The CGI expert kept everything simple and on point – hearing the speculation regarding the name of the new tiny EV , they imagined how the production version of this ultra-compact model could look based on the Every1 concept. Even better, the author also cooked up a GTI version to join the real world’s ID. Polo GTI at a lower price point. So, what do you think – yay or nay?
